en: Gregorio
"GBOHH!?{w}Y-you...{w}What the hell're you doin' to your precious only son, ya..."{w}
note: She has just hit him. The source cuts off mid-verb (nani shiyaga...); English trails off at the end instead, since the word order differs.

en: "Quit talking like that!{w}You're shaming me in front of the neighbors!"{w}
note: Source ends with ?! (rhetorical 'won't you?'); rendered as a statement.

en:
"W-well theeen...{w}YOU GUYS OVER THEEERE!
Lend me some cash, dammiiit!!"{w}
note: He turns on the party. The \n is kept as an emphatic break. | Editorial: jaa saa = 'well then' (no added 'fine'); 'you lot' is Armitt's tag, Gregorio's rocker voice gets 'you guys'.

en: "How many times do I have to tell you not to go bothering other people!!"{w}

"GYABOOOOH!?
S-sorry 'bout that..."{w}
note: Another blow lands. \n kept for the cry-then-apology beat.

en:
"Hmph!
And I told you to wipe off that makeup too -- it looks filthy!"{w}
note: Editorial: comma splice -> dash.

en:
"I-it ain't filthy!
It's cool! This makeup is totally raaad, yeahhhh!!"{w}
note: 'yeahhhh' renders the stretched emphatic da zeeee; rocker swagger.

en: "This boy is such an idiot!!"{w}
"MUGYOROPEPOOOH!?"{w}
note: Nonsense pain cry, romanized.

en:
"Honestly, you...
Get a job already, for goodness' sake.{w}How long are you planning to keep sponging off your parents?"{w}
note: Sune wo kajiru = sponge off one's parents, as in 4548.

en: "Go over to Walmitt's and get yourself some work.{w}Otherwise you'll end up an adult who can't do a single thing, you hear?"{w}
note: Walmitt's gender is unknown: 'Walmitt's' (their place) avoids a pronoun.

en: "I'm gonna keep the heart of a boy forever and..."{w}
note: Cut off (presumably another blow, no line between).

en: "O-okaaay, I gotchaaa...{w}Dammiiiiit!"{w}
note: Wakkarimassha = slurred 'wakarimashita' (understood).

en: Gregorio left.{w}
note: Editorial: 'went off' reads as exploding/flaring up; satte itta = left.

en: Gregorio's Voice
note: Glossary form.

en:
"Get off my back, ya damn old haaag!
My mom's got an outie belly buttonnnn!!"{w}
note: Debeso: the childish taunt 'your mom has an outie navel', which he aims at his own mother ('ore no kaachan'). Kept 'my mom' for the joke. | Accuracy: kuso-babaa carries kuso; crusty softened it, damn restores the force.

en: "Hey! No supper for you!!{w}...Sorry you had to see that embarrassing scene."{w}{p}"That was Gregorio.{w}He's a good kid at heart, though..."{w}
note: Editorial: stray comma made it read as an excuse, not an apology.

en: "I wonder if Gregorio really did get some work from Walmitt."{w}
"You haven't seen Gregorio, have you?"{w}
note: Editorial: subject restored (pro-drop rule).

en: "No matter how he mouths off, that boy always comes home at mealtimes..."{w}{p}"I've got a bad feeling about this.{w}All of you, if you come across Gregorio on your travels, tell him to come home, would you?"{w}
note: 'Minna' = the party addressed as a group.

en: "Honestly... where could he have gone..."{w}
"MAAAAAA!!"{w}
note: Kaachan = Mom/Ma.

en: "Gregorio, where on earth have you been!!"{w}
"I'm sorryyyy!{w}For your birthdaaay, Ma,{w}I got you thiiiis!!"{w}
Gregorio handed over an oven mitt.{w}
note: Nabetsukami = 'oven mitt', matching Armitt's 'ratty oven mitt' in 4550 (slice_019). Narration only; not an inventory item in this row.

en: "Why, this is...!!{w}I'm happy, but you... this..."{w}
note: She trails off; the next line answers how he paid for it, so no added question.
Wattari warararetari = 'splitting and being split', a joke; kept literal. \n kept for the list rhythm.

en: "Is that so... Thank you!!"{w}
"Ehehehehhh!!"{w}
The two of them are laughing happily.{w}
note: Present tense as in the source.

en: "Ever since then, Gregorio's turned into a real good boy."{w}{p}"It's all thanks to you lot.{w}Thank you."{w}
note: 'You lot' for anta-tachi, as in 4546.

en: "Huh...{w}Gregori...o...?"{w}{p}"No, but why...{w}Don't tell me he went to that Heerdahl Walmitt was talking about!?"{w}
note: Bad-outcome branch: something (likely his remains or news of his death) has been shown to her; the source does not say what. 'He went' restored from the elided verb.

en: "Ahhhh!{w}It's because I stuck my nose in!{w}Gregorio... my Gregoriooo!!"{w}
note: Yokei na koto wo shita = 'I did something I shouldn't have' (pushing him to get work). 'My Gregorio' renders the repeated, wailed name.

en: Armitt broke down in tears where she stood.{w}{p}Unable to find any words for her, you had no choice but to leave.{w}
Benef
"Here at Yotel Wharf, there's plenty for the fish to eat and plenty of places for them to hide, y'see.{w}Makes it a fine fishing spot, it does."{w}
note: Old-man speech (washi, -ja, -nou) given a light folksy register. Benef's gender is unknown in the glossary; no pronoun used.

en: "Oh... Here it comes!!{w}Hnnngh... THERE!!"{w}

Benef pulled on the rod...{w}{p}{0E}
          *    A tasty-looking fish!    *          {0F}{w}
note: Centered banner: full-width spaces replaced with ASCII spaces as in slice_006 (approximate centering); the full-width star kept as '*'.

en: Muse
"Sniff, sniff... Nya?"{w}
The girl who had been sleeping nearby slowly sat up.{w}
note: Mukuri to = getting up slowly or lazily, not with a start.

en: "Eep!!"{w}
"I smell food, nya~{w}Benef, did you catch something yummy again, nya?"{w}
"I didn't, I didn't catch a thing, Muse!"{w}
"Li~ar~ nyaaaaan~{w}You can't fool Muse's nose, nya!"{w}{p}"Gimme that~"{w}
note: Muse refers to herself as 'Muse'. Note ~ replaces the music note per convention.

en: "S-stay awaaay~~~"{w}

{0E}
              *  Whoops  *              {0F}{w}
note: Oootto = 'whoops' (Wizardry trap-message parody). Next slice has the variant oottotto; suggest 'Whoops-a-daisy'. Centering approximate.

en: "Aaaaahhh!!"{w}
Before Benef could reel the fish in, Muse snatched it right off the rod!{w}
"It's miiine, nyaaa!!"{w}
note: Itadaki = 'I'll take that'.

en:
"Chomp... munch munch... Mmm! Yummy!
Yum-nyan-nyan~"{w}
note: Umanyannyan = 'umai' (tasty) + cat sounds; music note -> ~.

en: "M...y... little... fishy...?"{w}
note: The source splits 'washi' (my) across a pause; English splits 'my'. O-sakana-san = cutesy 'fishy'.

en:
"Fwaaah..."{w}{p}"Tummy's full, so now Muse is all sleepy, nya.
Zzzz~..."{w}
note: Subject restored as 'Muse' to keep her third-person self-reference.

en: "Oh my, Benef, she got you again, did she?"{w}
note: Armitt (same washerwoman) appears in this scene too. 'She' = Muse (female per glossary).

en:
"Heh... heh heh heh..."{w}{p}"Here at Yotel Wharf...{w}there's plenty for the fish to eat and plenty of places for them to hide...{w}Makes it a fine fishing spot, it doooes..."{w}{p}"If only Muse weren't here...!
*sniff*..."{w}
note: Echoes 4629 word for word, broken up.

en: "For as long as I can remember, I've been dropping my line at this wharf to catch something to go with that day's rice."{w}{p}"But ever since I gave Muse a fish on a whim, she eats every one I catch."{w}
note: Okazu = side dish eaten with rice; set up here for 4665. Benef shifts to polite speech (orimashita, mashite) when telling the party. | Editorial: avoids two back-to-back 'ever since' openings (next page); progressive for the habitual action.

en: "For ten-odd years now, I've eaten nothing but sad, lonely meals with nothing to go with the rice.{w}That's why I keep telling myself, this time, this time for sure..."{w}
Benef's rod got a bite!!{w}
note: Sao ga hannou shita = the rod twitched / got a bite.

en: "So far, so normal...{w}It's after I reel it in that the trouble starts... it is!"{w}
Muse slowly sat up.{w}
"Not again!!"{w}
"I smell yummy fish, nya~{w}Benef, did you catch something yummy yet again, nya?"{w}
"W-wait, Muse!"{w}{p}"Just today, just this once, let me off!!{w}Ever since you showed up, I haven't had one decent meal..."{w}
note: Source breaks off mid-sentence; English trails off. | Accuracy: minogashite kure = spare me / let me off (he begs Muse); let it go could read as letting go of the fish.

en: "No~ can~ do~ nyaaaaan~{w}Muse's tummy shows no mercy, nya!"{w}{p}"Gimme that~"{w}
note: Dame = 'no way'; music note -> ~.

en: "S-stoooop~~~"{w}
"Again... my dinner..."{w}
note: Fragment kept. | Editorial: Benef's banmeshi = 'dinner', as in slice_021 (4751, 4777, 4815) and the corpus.

en: "Fwaaah..."{w}
Muse fell asleep.{w}
"Oh my, Benef, she got you yet again, did she?"{w}
note: Mirrors 4659 (matamata = yet again).

en: "Heh... heh heh heh..."{w}{p}"This... this right here is the cruel tale of Yotel Wharf...{w}Hnnnghhh~!!"{w}
note: Kufuu = a choked, tearful groan.

en: "My dinner...{w}My... dinnerrr... Ah, aaahhh..."{w}
note: Editorial: banmeshi = 'dinner', as in slice_021.

en: Benef keeps repeating it, as if delirious.{w}{p}Benef's rod got a bite!!{w}
note: Present tense as in the source.

en:
"This time I'll catch it... I'll show you I can...!!
I've worked out a secret plaaan!!"{w}
"Here you come!!"{w}
note: Kita na = 'so you've come / here it comes'. Read as Benef greeting Muse (she wakes and speaks next; the shared wake-up narration rows are deduplicated). Could instead be the bite: 'Here it comes!!'. | Accuracy: confirmed. Full SCDWMAP order is 4705 bite banner, 4707 Muse sniffs, 4708 Muse sits up, then 4710; the bite already happened, so the line greets Muse. | Editorial: Muse was asleep right beside him, so 'So you came' (an arrival from elsewhere) misfires; 'Here you come' keeps kita and the challenge.

en: "I smell yummy fish, nya~{w}Benef, thanks for catching fish for Muse every day, nyan!"{w}
"Hey, Muse!{w}Take a good look at what I've got here!"{w}
note: Temoto = what is in his hands (the two rods, next row).

en: "Nya?"{w}
"How about that? Today I'm fishing with two rods!{w}You've done nothing but sleep, so you'll never know which one has the fish on it!!"{w}
"It's true, nya! There's two rods!?{w}Which one's got the fish stuck on it, nya~?"{w}
